Updated quarterly with open data and software, the IGVF Catalog provides a scalable resource for variant-to-function discovery.

papers.title: Deciphering state bridges via a single-cell large language model
papers.abstract: Large-scale single-cell transcriptomic data provide a new avenue for precision medicine by uncovering cellular heterogeneity. However, systematic comparison of remodeling patterns across various biological states remains unavailable. Here, we first developed a computational framework based on a foundation model of single cell biology, Universal Cell Embedding (UCE), to harmonize annotations comprising 36 cell types. Based on an integrated dataset of single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with 8,789 human samples comprising more than 59 million cells or nuclei across 614 biological states, we then embedded each state with a 36-dimensional vector in a unified space of cell-composition change and further deciphered states bridges by analyzing the relationships among the 614 state vectors. As a result, 22,161 significant bridges (P < 0.05) between the 614 states were revealed. Moreover, we successfully identified a number of well-known bridges such as bridge between Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease (P = 2.21e-15), suggesting the effectiveness of the proposed framework. More importantly, we uncovered a number of new bridges. Furthermore, analyses of the number of changed cell types (NCC) and Shannon entropy revealed heterogeneous and tissue-dependent patterns of cellular composition remodeling. This study provides a new strategy for identifying disease associations and potential therapeutic relationships by deciphering bridges between biological states from scRNA-seq landscape.

papers.title: Genomic foundation models and complementary variant-scoring strategies in LGMD-associated genes: architecture, adaptation, and sequence context
papers.abstract: Genomic foundation models learn representations from DNA sequence, although their usefulness for variant classification depends on the architecture and downstream evaluation procedure. We compared six genomic foundation models using 6,960 ClinVar single-nucleotide variants from ten limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD)-associated genes, with 4,866 variants assigned to training and 2,094 to held-out testing. The analyses included frozen alternate-minus-reference embeddings at 101, 201 and 501 bp, supervised adaptation at 101 bp, and gene-held-out downstream classifier training. GPN-Star V100 and AlphaGenome Atlas AVI were evaluated separately using their native scores. At 101 bp, frozen Evo2 achieved the highest discrimination among the six foundation models (MCC 0.644; AUROC 0.879; AUPRC 0.818). Supervised adaptation increased MCC for three architectures and reduced it for the remaining three. Extending sequence context to 501 bp improved all three primary metrics in five of six frozen architectures, with Evo2 reaching an MCC of 0.864, AUROC of 0.964 and AUPRC of 0.952. Evo2 also led the frozen gene-held-out readouts (pooled MCC 0.641; AUROC 0.852; AUPRC 0.789). GPN-Star V100 and AVI achieved MCC values of 0.929 and 0.938, respectively, using distinct biological inputs and scoring procedures. The number of variants misclassified across all evaluated configurations decreased from five under the original 101-bp readouts to one after including longer contexts and native scores. An exploratory HGVS-category control identified substantial annotation-associated structure in the benchmark labels. The findings characterize classification performance against aggregate ClinVar labels within LGMD-associated genes. Disease-specific pathogenicity and clinical diagnostic utility remain untested.

papers.title: MAPLE: A hierarchical Multimodal Assistant for Pathology vision-Language Evaluation using logic and reasoning
papers.abstract: Pathological diagnosis requires integration of cellular morphology, tissue architecture, and clinical context across gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs), yet existing vision-language models remain constrained to patch-based analysis with resource-intensive architectures unsuitable for routine clinical deployment. Here we introduce MAPLE, a hierarchical pathology vision-language model that performs whole-slide diagnosis and report generation through efficient multi-scale reasoning. MAPLE employs AgenTile, a small 10-million-parameter vision transformer for cellular-level triage at 40x resolution, achieving segmentation performance equivalent to ~65-fold larger models (e.g., CellViT++) while providing ~95-fold faster inference. Cross-magnification integration with a CLIP-based image encoder at 10x and 5x enables recursive selection of the most diagnostically informative regions per slide. On the PathMMU benchmark (7691 image-question pairs), MAPLE's multimodal (image and text) reasoning module is the first to exceed pathologist performance across all four diagnostic domains (PubMed, EduContent, SocialPath, and Atlas), achieving 70.6-81.2% accuracy versus 68.3-72.9% for pathologists. MAPLE demonstrates calibrated clinical reasoning, appropriately expressing uncertainty for metastatic carcinoma requiring ancillary testing while providing a confident diagnosis for benign hamartoma. These results were validated using an additional clinical cohort. Taken together, our findings establish MAPLE as a computationally efficient, clinically deployable system for AI-augmented pathology, particularly suited to resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Integrating CRISPRi perturbation responses and transcription-factor binding priors for regulatory network inference in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.abstract: Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) represents an aggressive breast cancer subtype that lacks actionable cell-surface receptors, restricting frontline systemic management to cytotoxic chemotherapy. While recent functional epigenomics shows that TNBC progression is governed by non-coding regulatory remodeling at distal super-enhancers, conventional Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) inference methods rely on observational transcriptomic co-expression, which suffers from technical dropouts and confounding correlations that inflate false discoveries (>30%). Here, we present an interventional network inference framework that integrates large-scale single-cell CRISPR-interference perturbation sequencing (Perturb-seq; GSE224986, 95,678 cells across 11,975 sgRNAs) with ENCODE Factorbook ChIP-seq physical transcription factor binding priors across 819 somatic mutation-associated enhancer loci in human TNBC (MDA-MB-231). Our pipeline reconstructed a tripartite network yielding 5,935 physical TF-enhancer edges, 383,757 functional enhancer-gene edges, and 542,760 unique TF-target gene functional pairs across 372 active enhancers. Topological centrality prioritized master transcriptional drivers governing TNBC oncogenic signaling, including CTCF, POLR2A, EP300, JUND, MYC, and FOS, which regulate Hallmark programs for Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (p = 1.2 x 10-9) and cell cycle progression. Explainable machine learning (SHAP TreeExplainer) revealed non-linear, thresholded transactivation dynamics for AP-1 and MYC. Quantitative benchmarking against held-out CRISPRi ground truth demonstrated strong discriminatory accuracy (AUROC = 0.8999, AUPRC = 0.8745, Precision = 90.13%, FDR = 9.87%), substantially outperforming GENIE3 (AUPRC = 0.6323, FDR = 35.73%) and co-expression correlation (AUPRC = 0.6814). In silico-simulated driver feature silencing correlated with experimental responses (R2 = 0.473, p < 10-122), and master driver signatures significantly stratified overall survival in the METABRIC (n = 320) and TCGA-BRCA (n = 160; p [≤] 0.019) cohorts. Finally, in silico perturbation modeling indicated that multi-target epigenetic combinations achieved 93% topological disruption of oncogenic regulatory connectivity, nominating prioritized candidate circuits for experimental validation.

papers.title: Vir2vec: A Genome-Wide Viral Embedding
papers.abstract: Genomic language models (gLMs) enable the extraction of meaningful numerical representations from DNA sequences, yet existing approaches primarily focus on human genomes or limited viral datasets, and systematic evaluations of viral representations remain scarce. Here, we introduce Vir2vec, a family of decoder-only gLMs (from 17M to 422M parameters) continually pretrained on a curated viral corpus comprising 565,747 complete genomes and genomic segment records assigned to 295 different species. We also present the viral Genome Understanding Evaluation (vGUE), a seven-task evaluation suite assessing viral representations across broad organism discrimination, evolutionary signatures, intra-genus species classification, variant subtyping, and host-associated phenotypes. Evaluated as a frozen feature extractor under nested cross-validation, Vir2vec achieves the highest balanced accuracy on three of seven tasks (full-genome virus detection, DNA-versus-RNA classification, and host-category prediction) and shares the highest performance on HIV-1 versus HIV-2 classification, while alternative models lead on the remaining three tasks. Taxonomic exclusion experiments further assess generalization of classification capabilities when an RNA-virus clade is excluded from pretraining at species and family levels. Finally, we introduce an argmax-routed SHAP explainability framework that maps feature attributions to codon-level sequence coordinates, highlighting receptor-binding-domain positions associated with SARS-CoV-2 human-versus-mouse host specificity discrimination. Together, Vir2vec and vGUE provide resources for advancing viral genomic representation learning and its systematic evaluation.

papers.title: A transcriptomic-driven segmentation and cell simulation framework for high-resolution spatial transcriptomics and cell-cell communication
papers.abstract: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics platforms, such as Visium HD and Atera, enable transcriptome-wide profiling at near-single-cell resolution. However, accurate cell segmentation to define spatial boundaries relies heavily on histological images. Previous approaches struggle in tissues with high cell density, inflammation, or mineralization, leading to transcriptomic bleed-through and inaccurate clustering. To address this, we developed TENGU (Transcript-signal Enrichment and Grouping Unit), a comprehensive end-to-end bioinformatic software package. Unlike existing tools, TENGU employs a transcript-first segmentation approach, prioritizing transcript-signal density as the primary modality and utilizing histological images only as a secondary supplement in unresolved regions. These initial boundaries are further optimized through a transcriptomic-driven cell simulation algorithm that iteratively refines boundaries based on localized gene expression probabilities, effectively minimizing spatial scattering and preserving biologically distinct molecular signatures. The pipeline seamlessly integrates tissue segmentation, high-resolution cell-type annotation, and spatially aware cell-cell communication (CCC) analysis. We rigorously benchmarked TENGU against the 10x Genomics and Bin2cell pipelines for segmentation, and against CellNEST for spatial CCC inference, across diverse and technically challenging microenvironments. TENGU demonstrated superior transcriptomic distinctness in the murine brain and successfully captured matrix-embedded osteocytes in decalcified bone. In murine osteomyelitis, TENGU outperformed CellNEST in sensitivity, localizing both reactive bone remodeling (Tgfb) and dense, abscess-encapsulating inflammatory (Il1a/Il1) networks. TENGU also resolved species-specific pro-tumorigenic hubs (MDK-SDC4) in a human colorectal cancer xenograft and generalized effectively to the Atera platform, delineating CXCL12-CXCR4 and LGALS3-TGFBR2 signaling within highly compacted human breast cancer tissue. By mitigating image-dependent constraints, TENGU provides a highly adaptable, robust computational framework to decode the functional micro-anatomy of healthy and pathological tissues.

papers.title: HealthFound: a health world model for quantitative reasoning on longitudinal health profiles
papers.abstract: Medical large language models have shown promise in medical knowledge retrieval and clinical reasoning but remain limited in quantitative reasoning over longitudinal health data, partly due to the lack of effective data construction and model training strategies tailored to large-scale prospective cohorts. Here, we present HealthFound, a health world model trained on 12.4 million constructed examples, including 14-year longitudinal biomedical records from 501,936 participants and datasets for medical knowledge and general reasoning. We propose a three-stage training framework comprising progressive curriculum supervised fine-tuning, rejection-sampled retention fine-tuning, and task-verifiable policy optimization. This enables the model to effectively parse heterogeneous quantitative data and perform robust quantitative reasoning about incident diseases and health trajectories. HealthFound achieves the highest mean accuracy across eight public medical benchmarks. On the task of predicting 1,074 future disease onsets, it outperforms the closest large language model by approximately 10 percentage points on average. In two independent external validations (MIMIC-IV and NHANES), it demonstrates superior zero-shot generalization, achieving improvements of over 5.2% across 417 disease endpoints. The model also achieves top results on tasks involving literature-derived question answering and quantitative indicator imputation. Furthermore, HealthFound generates interpretable reasoning rationales that are consistent with established biomedical knowledge. Collectively, our results demonstrate that HealthFound enables medical LLMs to evolve from static knowledge repositories into dynamic quantitative reasoning engines over longitudinal health data.

papers.title: Hitchhiker bias can distort inference of pathogen severity and pathogen-pathogen interactions from symptom-based surveillance: A modeling study
papers.abstract: Symptom-based infectious disease surveillance, which infers pathogen circulation by testing individuals who seek care for clinical symptoms, is widely used in public health but can distort our understanding of pathogen dynamics. Detecting a pathogen in a hospitalized patient does not establish that it caused the hospitalization. When a mildly pathogenic virus is detected in patients hospitalized because of a co-infecting, more pathogenic virus, the hospitalization can be wrongly attributed to the mild virus, a mechanism we term hitchhiker bias. Building on the aetiology-attribution literature, we couple this misattribution to a two-pathogen SEIR model with explicit co-infection and multiplex observation, and ask how an unmodeled incidental-detection pathway is absorbed into the parameters estimated by transmission models. We show that the relative inflation of observed hospitalizations is governed by the ratio of the two viruses' hospitalization probabilities and by the fraction of mild-virus infections that are co-infections. In simulation-estimation experiments, ignoring the hitchhiker pathway overestimated the hospitalization probability of the mild virus about 3-fold under partial and 7-fold under complete epidemic overlap, with credible intervals that excluded the true value. In the absence of biological interaction, it also overestimated the mild virus's reproduction number and generated spurious inhibition under partial overlap, and generated spurious facilitation under complete overlap. When the viruses truly interacted, the bias in the estimated interaction depended on epidemic overlap: a true inhibition appeared stronger under partial overlap but was reversed into weak facilitation under complete overlap, and a true facilitation appeared stronger. Explicitly modeling the hitchhiker pathway recovered hospitalization probabilities and interaction strengths when the observation model was correctly specified. These results highlight the importance of separating pathogen-attributable hospitalization from incidental detection when drawing epidemiological inferences from symptom-based surveillance.

papers.title: The unedited acceptance rate: a review-fidelity metric for human-in-the-loop clinical AI
papers.abstract: Objective. Guidance for large language model (LLM) drafting in clinical care relies on human review, yet review is rarely measured as a control. We aimed to define computable measures of review fidelity, establish which a deployed system can compute, and pre-specify their first analysis. Materials and Methods. For a multi-agent clinical system in routine use at one private London outpatient clinic, we defined acceptance coverage, attribution completeness, the unedited acceptance rate (UAR), a bounded normalized edit distance, availability latency and an unedited fast-approval rate (UFA). We checked each measure against the system's code and database structure at a fixed commit on four approval routes and pre-specified a prospective 12-week analysis. Results. The UAR equals the mass at zero of the edit-distance distribution, and availability latency bounds reading time from above only. Clinical documentation keeps draft and signed text with a recorded signer, so the core measures are computable there. Help-desk edit telemetry is written only when the agent's version has been stored. The WhatsApp agent route records no edit signal, and its approver need not be named. No route records when a draft is opened. Documentation accept events were not written before a change committed on November 16, 2026. Model-generated content, including live voice-agent speech, also reaches patients without approval. No measured values are reported. Discussion. Acceptance alone cannot separate accurate drafts from approval without reading, and three of four routes cannot yet support the family. Conclusion. Review fidelity can be specified as telemetry at the approval event. Validation against missed errors is required.

papers.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Autism ADOS-2 Calibrated Severity Scores Using Genetic and Behavioral Features
papers.abstract: Background: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition characterized by social communication difficulties and restricted, repetitive behaviors. While machine learning has been widely applied in autism research, few studies have predicted continuous autism severity measures such as the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule Calibrated Severity Score (ADOS CSS). We evaluated behavioral and genetic predictors of ADOS CSS across ADOS modules. Methods: Participants from the Simons Simplex Collection who completed ADOS Modules 1, 2, or 3 were included. Behavioral questionnaire data and gene-level measures of loss-of-function intolerance (pLI, LOEUF) and brain-expression specificity (pExt) were used to train 12 machine learning models separately for each module. Performance was evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE), Pearson correlation (r), and SHAP analyses. Results: Ensemble-based models achieved the strongest performance across modules. In Module 1, adding genetic predictors improved Random Forest performance (MAE 1.189 to 1.051; r 0.204 to 0.340). Module 2 achieved the highest overall performance, with XGBoost reaching r {approx} 0.49 and MAE = 1.010. SHAP analyses showed that genetic predictors contributed most strongly in Module 1, whereas predictions for Module 3 were driven primarily by verbal, behavioral, and social-cognitive features. Conclusions: Integrating genetic and behavioral features improved ADOS CSS prediction, particularly in children with limited expressive language. Genetic information was most informative in Module 1, while behavioral and social-cognitive measures became increasingly important in later developmental stages, consistent with evidence that genetic burden is more strongly associated with greater developmental impairment.

papers.title: Viral discovery using untargeted metagenomics and complementary proteomics in plasma cell-rich virus-like tubulointerstitial nephritis after kidney transplantation
papers.abstract: Background Kidney allograft biopsies may show plasma cell-rich tubulointerstitial inflammation and tubular epithelial changes suggestive of viral infection despite negative routine testing for known viruses. Whether this plasma cell-rich virus-like tubulointerstitial nephritis (PCR-TIN) is associated with an unrecognized viral agent is unknown. Methods We retrospectively identified 57 kidney allograft biopsies with a plasma cell-rich tubulointerstitial phenotype. Frozen tissue from 34 biopsies and matched urine from 14 cases underwent virus discovery cDNA-amplified fragment length polymorphism next-generation sequencing (VIDISCA-NGS). BK polyomavirus-associated nephropathy (BKPyVAN) tissue served as a positive control for viral detection in renal tissue. Data-independent acquisition parallel accumulation-serial fragmentation liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry was used to evaluate the feasibility of detecting BK polyomavirus peptides. In an exploratory secondary analysis, host-protein abundance and Hallmark pathway enrichment were compared among 11 PCR-TIN, 91 other rejection, and 20 BKPyVAN biopsies. Results In positive-control experiments, VIDISCA-NGS detected BK polyomavirus at 13 of 216,879 reads (0.006%) and, after DNase treatment, at 5 of 81,614 reads (0.006%). Across the 34 PCR-TIN biopsies, 3,751,011 reads were generated (mean, 110,324 per biopsy). Sporadic low-level anelloviruses and Merkel cell polyomavirus reads (<10 reads per positive specimen) were detected in five and four biopsies, respectively, but no consistent candidate pathogenic viral agent was identified. Similarly, no candidate pathogenic viral agent associated with PCR-TIN was identified among 409,563 reads from the 14 matched urine samples (mean, 29,255 per sample). Proteomic interrogation did not detect BK polyomavirus peptides even in proven BKPyVAN, rendering this approach technically inconclusive for viral detection in PCR-TIN. Six proteins were significantly more abundant in PCR-TIN than in other rejection, whereas none differed significantly between PCR-TIN and BKPyVAN. Compared with both groups, PCR-TIN showed enrichment of epithelial-mesenchymal transition, interferon-response, allograft-rejection, inflammatory, and unfolded-protein-response programs, whereas oxidative phosphorylation and several metabolic pathways were enriched in the comparator groups. Conclusion Repeated VIDISCA-NGS of kidney tissue and matched urine did not identify a candidate pathogenic viral agent associated with PCR-TIN. These findings make a prevalent virus detectable by this workflow less likely but do not exclude low-abundance, focal, transient, or methodologically inaccessible infection. Exploratory host proteomics identified inflammatory, cellular-stress, and tissue-remodeling programs associated with PCR-TIN, but these findings characterize the accompanying host response, not its cause.
